stemBlocks.value: The force F acting on an object varies directly as its acceleration a. Given that F = 18 when a = 6, find the value of F when a = 10.
Think first: Force divided by acceleration is a fixed constant, so one pair of values unlocks the rest.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p115-q05 from workbook page 115.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the variation statement as an equation.
Substitute F = 18 and a = 6 to find k.

strategyBlocks.value: Write F = ka, find k from F = 18 and a = 6, then substitute a = 10.

whyThisWorks.value: The constant k is the mass of the object, which does not change as the acceleration changes. That is why F ÷ a gives the same value for every pair, and why a single measurement is enough to predict the force at any other acceleration.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying 18 by 10 without first dividing by 6.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying 18 by 10 without first dividing by 6.

commonErrors.misconception: Confusing which quantity is the subject when writing F = ka.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Confusing which quantity is the subject when writing F = ka.

commonErrors.misconception: Assuming F increases by 10 because a increased by 4.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Assuming F increases by 10 because a increased by 4.

examTip.value: Set out direct variation in three lines every time — equation, find k, substitute — so no step is skipped under exam pressure.
